newsitem.title: ITALY: Bell Atlantic snatches Omnitel stake.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic snatches Omnitel stake.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Monday clinched a deal to increase its stake in Italy's mobile phone group Omnitel, dashing at the last moment German group's Mannesmann's hopes.

Omnitel's largest shareholder Olivetti said in a statement that Bell had exercised its pre-emptive rights to buy the 8.26 percent stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari (OSR) that Mannesmann believed it had closed last month.

Olivetti, the money-losing Italian information and technology group, had put the OSR stake up for sale to help cut its hefty debts and restructure its troubled portfolio of computer and telecommunications businesses. Olivetti is the major shareholder in OSR, which in turn owns 70 percent of Italy's second mobile phone operator Omnitel.

An Olivetti spokesman confirmed the deal had been completed and Philadelphia-based Bell Atlantic would buy the 8.26 percent stake in OSR -- or a 5.8 percent indirect stake in Omnitel -- on the same terms as Mannesmann agreed, that is to pay 432.5 billion lire ($283 million).

Last month, Mannesmann which was already a shareholder in Omnitel, signed a contract to buy the 8.26 percent stake from Olivetti, but as required by the by-laws of OSR, the sale was subject to pre-emptive rights of the other shareholders.

These shareholders included Swedish state-owned telecommunications operator Telia, U.S. Cellular Communications International Inc. (CCIL), as well as Bell and Olivetti. They had 30 days to exercise their rights on the same terms as stipulated in the Mannesmann contract which was to be activated in early to mid November.

Olivetti confirmed that Bell, which already had a 16.9 percent stake in OSR, was exercising its right to buy the stake, bringing its total up to 24.9 percent, while other OSR partners CCIL and Telia had not exercised their rights.
